messages:
jordan: heads-up — just hit a flurry of microreleases that tripped the deploy bot timeout during the midnight change window. deploy-bot aborted 3 canaries in a row. :(

alex: ugh. which canaries? service-a or infra-only?

jordan: service-a and service-b, but the PRs were telemetry-flag flips + lockfile updates (no prod code).

deploy-bot: System: attempted deploy 3x -> timeout. Logs: `ERR_TIMEOUT_CANARY=120s` -> aborted.

priya: are these eligible for a patch bump only? my read: flag flip + lockfile => patch, but releasebot sometimes forces minor when metadata present.

marc: agreed patch for behaviorless changes. The problem is our releasebot heuristics: if changelog exists it bumps minor unless PR has label `docs|infra-only`. We should tighten that.

alex: we also have timing issue: microreleases queued back-to-back exceed concurrent deploys quota -> race and timeouts. Maybe cap parallel canaries to 2 for change-window.

jordan: current quick proposal: 1) treat flag-only + lockfile as patch automatically 2) if deploy-bot sees >2 concurrent canaries from same change window, serialize them 3) don't treat presence of a free-form changelog file as auto-minor.

ops: serialization makes sense. Also add guard for `release-notes-bot` generated entries: if bot wrote the changelog, trust label `changelog:auto` to keep patch.

release-notes-bot: Note: when `changelog:auto` present I can add `meta:generated=true` in the PR body. We can parse that instead of relying on file text heuristics.

priya: semver edgecase question: what about builds that only change `buildmeta` suffix like `1.2.3+ci.45`? Do we keep version or emit a patch?

marc: buildmeta changes should not bump semver for consumers; they are ignored by semver precedence. For our release ledger we can attach a new buildmeta marker but keep the public tag `1.2.3`. Only bump patch if contents actually change.

alex: rollback decision — if deploy-bot aborts canary due to timeout, should we auto-rollback previous production? Current behavior: no auto-rollback, just pause. I vote for automated rollback only when health-check errors (non-timeout) or >50% canaries failed.

jordan: +1. Timeouts are noisy. We should surface alerts and auto-serialize retries but avoid rollback unless explicit failed checks.

ops: action items I'll track: `GH-ops-112` add `canary_parallel_limit` config per change-window; `GH-ops-113` parse `meta:generated=true` from release-notes-bot; `GH-ops-114` change releasebot bump heuristics to prefer patch for flag/lockfile-only PRs.

priya: tiny nit — add a PR label `semver:force-patch` that authors can apply when automatic detection misfires. Also allow `semver:force-minor` for deliberate bumps.

deploy-bot: FYI: upcoming deploy config supports `--serialize-canaries=true` as runtime flag. Example: 
```
deploy-bot deploy --serialize-canaries --window=midnight
```

alex: thanks. We'll start with labels + serialization. Ops, can you gate deploy-bot retries so we don't spin forever? limit 3 attempts with backoff.

ops: yep. I'll put a backoff config: 30s -> 90s -> 180s, then pause and notify #incidents.

marc: one more: update the release notes checklist template to ask whether change modifies runtime behavior. That will reduce false minors.

jordan: perfect. thanks team. if nobody objects i'll merge the ops PRs after tests. :thumbsup:

alex: no objections from me. ship it when green.

deploy-bot: System: scheduled job created (GH-ops-112, GH-ops-113, GH-ops-114).
